chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a portion of his wealth. He said, 'A portion from ten.' He said, 'Allah the Exalted said, "Then place on each of them a portion" (Quran 11:82), and the mountains were ten mountains.'
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'a portion' (juz') mean in Islamic inheritance law according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ambiguous term 'portion' (juz') in bequests by linking it to the ten mountains mentioned in Surah Hud, verse 82. He interprets 'a portion' as one-tenth, establishing a legal precedent where vague fractional bequests are resolved through Quranic numerical analogies. This reflects the Shia scholarly method of deriving precise fiqh rulings from subtle linguistic cues in the Quran.
